title: Deep Memory · A catalogue of distant resemblances
scope: A first curated collection of claimed anomalies, with optional local and transmission controls. Not a completed worldwide survey.
date_convention: Signed historical years: -1 = 1 BCE, +1 = 1 CE; no year zero. Intervals include their endpoints. Dates retain their event type and uncertainty; a null range means unresolved.

sources.title: Teaching figures: primary-source audit

sources.title: Berossus through Eusebius, Chronicle I

sources.note: Colonial witness for Viracocha; the recording date is not the origin date of the tradition.

sources.note: Colonial witness for Bochica. The audited arrival is inland, not from the sea.

sources.title: Flood Tablet · K.3375

sources.title: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1: Manu and the fish

sources.title: Flood stories: text-coding pilot

sources.author: Deep Memory

sources.title: Ancient Rapanui genomes and contact with the Americas
sources.note: Ancient-genome evidence supports pre-European admixture dated about 1250–1430 CE. It does not establish a route for a particular motif.
sources.author: Moreno-Mayar et al., 2024

sources.title: South and Southeast Asian art: Indus trade
sources.note: Indus seals in Mesopotamian contexts and the reverse support exchange. A useful control for what independent contact evidence looks like.
sources.author: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

dates.label: 1688 CE · publication
dates.note: Colonial published witness, not an event or origin date.

dates.label: Date unresolved

dates.label: 7th century BCE · tablet
dates.note: Age of this material witness, not the beginning of the story.

entities.note: The preserved tablet carries a sequence of bird releases as well as a warning and a boat.
entities.text: A warning, a vessel, survival through a flood, then birds sent out to seek land.

entities.label: Manu and the fish

dates.label: Date unresolved
dates.note: An early composition range and manuscript witness history have not been audited for this entry.

entities.note: The inspected passage is Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1. A modern translation is a route to that text, not a date for the event.
entities.text: A fish warns Manu, has him prepare a boat, and guides it through the flood.

dates.note: Neolithic attribution is established in the discovery context; this review has not tied the individual carving to a dated stratum.

dates.note: Broad published site context. No direct measurement dates this individual motif.

entities.label: Seals across trading regions

dates.label: Bronze Age exchange · individual finds pending
dates.note: The source discusses exchanged seals. Individual find contexts and dated assemblages have not yet been entered, so no numerical range is assigned to this summary.

entities.note: The Met’s survey describes Indus seals found in Mesopotamian cities and Mesopotamian seals at Indus sites. This record summarises that evidence; it is not an individual object or a count of exchanged seals.
entities.text: Seals found outside their producing regions provide material evidence of exchange.

claims.title: Birdmen across two worlds
claims.dek: Birds, bent limbs and rounded forms, across a vast interval in place and time.
claims.anomaly: The recurring features invite a comparison between repertoires, rather than a single fortunate pairing. A historical link would have to bridge a very large chronology gap.
features: Both groups include bird imagery in complex carved or painted scenes.
The narrow bird-and-rounded-form correspondence is strongest for Pillar 43 and the Orongo boulder; it is not equally present in every group member.
differences: The Rapanui group includes human–bird hybrids; the Pillar 43 figure is generally described as a vulture.
The moai’s ring is below the birdmen; the boulder’s rounded object is at a bent hand; Pillar 43’s disc lies above a wing.
The group samples were selected for this inquiry. They do not establish how common or rare the combination is.

diffusion.note: No transmission sequence for this specific comparison has been established in the sources reviewed. That is not proof that contact was impossible.

origin.note: Starting comparison from the supplied project material; Lee Paqui’s 2024 article independently states the narrower bird-and-rounded-object parallel.

next_steps: Build dated local sequences on both sides.
Use expert-reviewed feature locations and relations before any similarity ranking.
Add a documented comparison corpus selected independently of the proposed match.

motifs.note: Teaching figures, sea journeys and the history of a retelling.

motifs.label: Floods & renewal
motifs.note: Warnings, vessels, surviving life and the search for land.

motifs.label: Monuments
motifs.note: Construction, geometry and the purpose of a building.

motifs.label: Animal sculpture
motifs.note: Specific creatures, uncertain captions and full-object comparisons.

motifs.label: Contact evidence
motifs.note: Independent evidence useful for testing a proposed transmission.

cultures.label: Neolithic Anatolia
cultures.note: Regional grouping, not a claim that every site or carving belongs to one homogeneous culture.

cultures.label: Rapanui traditions
cultures.note: Different media and episodes in Rapa Nui’s history. Statue construction, later carving, texts and modern records remain separate.

cultures.label: Assyrian imagery
cultures.note: A documented Neo-Assyrian palace context. Earlier Mesopotamian literature is a separate cluster.

cultures.label: Olmec La Venta
cultures.note: This edition represents La Venta with one monument; it cannot estimate variation across Olmec imagery.

cultures.label: Tiwanaku
cultures.note: A selected monumental figure; wider Andean traditions are not collapsed into this cluster.

cultures.label: Epiclassic Cacaxtla
cultures.note: A local painted repertoire within a connected Mesoamerican world.

cultures.label: Mississippian Cahokia
cultures.note: A provisional object lead, currently illustrated by a modern drawing.

cultures.label: Greek Delphi
cultures.note: The sacred-centre tradition and the date of the pictured museum object need separate sources.

cultures.label: Indus / Harappan
cultures.note: A geographically distributed corpus with changing phases, represented here by one museum example and a sign-study archive.

cultures.label: Jiroft region
cultures.note: Provisional regional attribution, not an excavated object context or a fully described culture.

cultures.label: Lingjiatan
cultures.note: A caption-based lead awaiting collection and excavation checks.

cultures.label: Arnhem Land · attribution open
cultures.note: A geographic lead, not one culture. Community, artist, site and chronology remain unresolved.

cultures.label: Mesopotamian accounts
cultures.note: Literary traditions with multiple periods and surviving witnesses; their recording dates do not date the narrated events.

cultures.label: Andean accounts
cultures.note: Selected colonial witness to a tradition whose earlier history needs separate evidence.

cultures.label: Nahua accounts
cultures.note: Sources shaped by Nahua collaborators and colonial recording; no single origin date is assigned.

cultures.label: Muisca accounts
cultures.note: A selected colonial source family, not the whole living or historical tradition.

cultures.label: Pohnpei · story untraced
cultures.note: An unverified narrative lead, not an authenticated catalogue of Pohnpeian tradition.

cultures.label: Vedic textual tradition
cultures.note: One inspected Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa episode; composition and manuscript chronology remain to be audited.

cultures.label: Old Kingdom Egypt
cultures.note: An architectural comparison lead awaiting its independent object-level source dossier.

cultures.label: Maya Chichén Itzá
cultures.note: A particular monument with multiple building phases, not all Maya architecture.

cultures.label: Americas · ancestry evidence
cultures.note: A research category, not a single culture. Exact ancestral locality is not asserted.

cultures.label: Identity still open
cultures.note: Unresolved records stay discoverable without invented cultural attribution.

cultures.label: Mesopotamian exchange contexts
cultures.note: A regional context for the documented Indus trade control. Individual finds and phases remain to be registered.
